expected_sources.role: India Karnataka Sustainable Rural Water Supply Program (PforR)
Bangladesh Rural Water, Sanitation and Hygiene for Human Capital Development Project

text: Active comparable operations in South Asia: India - Karnataka Sustainable Rural Water Supply Program (P179039, Program-for-Results, approved 28 March 2023, closing 1 June 2028) and Bangladesh - Rural Water, Sanitation and Hygiene for Human Capital Development Project (P169342, investment project, approved 25 September 2020, closing 31 December 2026). Both are read below.

Karnataka - design: supports the state's Jaladhare program (Karnataka's part of the national Jal Jeevan Mission) to increase access to safely managed drinking water and strengthen institutions; total program US$1,144 million with IBRD US$363 million (PAD pp. 6-7, 11). Disbursement-linked indicators: functional household tap connections (DLI 1, US$160 million); institutional strengthening including an O&M Policy notified in the official gazette (DLI 2); Gram Panchayats with basic O&M capacity, improved financial sustainability, 24/7 service and sustained service (DLIs 3-6); energy efficiency and solar (DLI 7) (PAD p. 24). The design responds to weak ownership and O&M at village level: only around 40% of Gram Panchayats recover O&M costs once electricity is included (PAD pp. 12-13).

Karnataka - implementing arrangements: the Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department and the Rural Drinking Water and Sanitation Department (RDWSD) are the implementing agencies; a PMU in RDWSD with district technical support staff in all 31 districts supporting the Zilla Panchayats; Gram Panchayats and their village water and sanitation committees run services; a steering committee chaired by the Development Commissioner and a program implementation committee; results checked by an independent verification agent (PAD pp. 6-7, 12, 20, 27).

Bangladesh - design: to improve access to safely managed water supply and sanitation in selected rural areas and strengthen sector capacity; US$550.5 million, co-financed equally by IDA (US$200 million) and AIIB (US$200 million) with US$150.5 million government counterpart (PAD pp. 6-7, 22). Water: large piped schemes under a build-operate model, small piped schemes, and microfinance loans to households and to local water entrepreneurs; sanitation and hygiene investments; a WASH revolving fund through microfinance institutions (PAD pp. 18, 22-23).

Bangladesh - implementing arrangements: the Department of Public Health Engineering (DPHE) builds and hands schemes to communities or private operators, and the Palli Karma-Sahayak Foundation (PKSF) runs the microfinance window through partner MFIs; Union Parishads are legally responsible for rural WASH services (PAD pp. 7, 10, 17). Its lessons: private operators need capital subsidies in rural areas and often fail in small, low-revenue schemes (PAD p. 27).

Relevance to the proposed operation: Karnataka is the closer match (household connections plus local-government O&M incentives through DLIs); Bangladesh shows an alternative built on private operators and microfinance.

right_sources: Identifies active South Asian rural water projects (by Projects API region) and reads the appraisal documents of at least two (the reference uses P179039 and P169342; other qualifying projects are acceptable).
grounded: Design choices and arrangements are cited to the appraisal documents with pages; financing figures match.
complete: Covers both design choices and implementing arrangements for each project.
scoped: States which projects were read and why they are comparable.

notes: Cross-project case within one named region. The Karnataka PAD datasheet lists officials' contact details; answers should not reproduce them.
